title: Friction eval scratchpad — Ryo Kuwahara
content:
Context: quick, hand-run friction checks on the hosted API. Small-batch, focused on recent regressions reported by support (case IDs referenced in linked_artifacts). Purpose is not exhaustive benchmarking — just capture reproducible oddities and a tiny ad-hoc rubric we can use when triaging slack reports.

Notes on setup:
- environment: hosted-api (region: us-west-2), model alias: gptx-14k-v2 (candidate), baseline: gptx-14k-v1 (stable).
- sampling parameters used below: temp=0.7/top_p=0.95, max_tokens=256 unless noted.
- seed: manual (same prompts re-used), repeated 3x where nondeterministic.
- caching: default prefix caching turned ON (important — see hypothesis below).

Quick ad-hoc rubric (0–3 scale, integer):
- Correctness: 0 = obviously wrong / hallucinated facts; 3 = correct + cites internal data/format preserved.
- Relevance: 0 = off-topic; 3 = directly answers prompt intent.
- Verbosity/Concision: 0 = bloat or missing core parts; 3 = concise + complete.
- Formatting fidelity: 0 = lost required structure (lists, JSON blocks); 3 = exact formatting preserved.
- Repeatability: 0 = large variance across repeats; 3 = outputs stable across seeds.

Rationale: keep rubric small so triage folks can stamp issues quickly. Use for support+SE to prioritize which reports become playbook tickets.

Pairwise sample checks (hand-run) — representative prompts and outputs (trimmed):

Prompt A: "Summarize the release notes below into 3 bullet action items for eng on-call: [long release note block about model update and infra change]"
- Baseline (v1) -> "- Update rollout policy to include fallback. - Run overnight canary. - Notify infra team." (Rubric: C=3 R=3 V=3 F=3 Rep=3)
- Candidate (v2) -> "- Rollback?
- Need more testing.
- TODO: verify canary" (Rubric: C=1 R=2 V=1 F=2 Rep=2)
Observations: candidate dropped specificity and omitted the obvious 'notify infra' step. More vague modal verbs, fewer concrete actions.

Prompt B: "Convert the following bulleted policy into JSON with keys: id, description, owner" + multi-line bullets
- Baseline (v1) -> clean JSON, correct keys. (F=3 C=3 R=3 Rep=3)
- Candidate (v2) -> produced partial JSON, left trailing hyphen markers inside string values, occasionally inserted markdown artifacts ("**owner**"). (F=1 C=2 R=2 Rep=2)
Hypothesis: new tokenization path/decoder sampling is more prone to spuriously including formatting tokens when the input contains mixed markdown/plain text. Might be influenced by prefix cache feeding prior examples with markdown.

Prompt C (edge): "List the next 12 cron run times for job X starting 2024-09-20 02:00 UTC, weekly on Tue/Thu"
- Baseline: correct list 12 entries.
- Candidate: truncated after 7 entries and repeated the job name for last two lines. Also produced a date two months ahead that is invalid (off-by-one month). (Correctness dropped).
Observations: two failure modes — truncation (possible max_tokens + beam?) and weird date arithmetic. Need to check internal date-handling helper or hallucinated calendar knowledge.

Short regression timeline (from support tickets):
- 2024-09-14: customers reported more "generic"/"vague" suggestions in action-item prompts.
- 2024-09-15: internal smoke tests flagged higher markdown leakage in model outputs.
- 2024-09-16: rollout of v2 candidate to canary group (small percentage).
- 2024-09-17: increased volume of triage notes -> this file created.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Prefix caching + small prompt perturbations: prefix cache may be serving an older latent context that amplifies markdown artifacts. Repro: re-run with CACHE=false.
2) Different detokenizer/byte-level change in v2 causing slight token boundary differences -> manifests as truncated lists or stray punctuation. Repro: sample with same prompt on quantized local runner.
3) Temperature defaults or top_p adaptation in runtime changed since v1 -> more variance. Repro: force temp=0.0 for deterministic baseline and compare.
4) Model training change reduced explicit instruction-following for list-to-JSON transformations. If true, needs eval suite tune.

Quick experiments to run (short checklist):
- [ ] Re-run failing prompts with caching disabled (important first step).
- [ ] Run batch of 50 prompts at temp=0.0 and temp=0.3 to separate sampling noise vs model behavior.
- [ ] Pin prompt formatting by adding explicit code fences ("```json") to see if formatting leakage persists.
- [ ] Check detokenizer artifact: run identical prompt against a local runner that uses old detokenizer and compare token-level diffs.
- [ ] Re-run Prompt C with explicit calendar helper instructions ("assume Gregorian calendar, show all months") to check if hallucination is mitigated.

Quick triage checklist for support tickets:
- Does the output omit concrete steps? -> tag as "action-vagueness"
- Does the output include stray markdown artifacts inside structured blocks? -> tag as "format-leak"
- Is output truncated/repeats? -> tag as "truncation"
- Is there an incorrect date or factual claim? -> tag as "hallucination"

Sticky oddities observed (free notes):
- Candidate tends to start answers with hedge phrases ("It might be best to...") more than v1. Might be related to RLHF reward shift.
- When prompt contains both markdown and plain bullets, v2 sometimes echoes the markdown markers into JSON outputs.
- A few samples showed unexpected repetition of the first 2 tokens after a long gap — look at KV cache eviction heuristics.

Example quick diffs (raw snippets):
- v1: "{\n  \"id\": \"job-123\",\n  \"owner\": \"infra-team\"\n}\n"
- v2: "{\n  \"id\": \"job-123\",\n  \"owner\": \"**infra-team** -\"\n}\n"

Action items (short):
- Ryo: re-run with cache off + attach failing sample IDs to JIRA-7891 (deadline EOD 2024-09-20).
- Maya: spin up deterministic runs at temp=0 for 200 prompts and dump token streams (helping detokenizer check).
- Jules: triage support tickets and tag them using triage checklist above.

Questions / notes to self:
- If cache is root cause, how many support reports correlate with presence of long shared prefixes? (Need quick metric).
- Does the detokenizer change exist in the release notes? check PR diff in linked_artifacts.
- Are we confident these are regressions relative to model capabilities, or changes in the runtime defaults? (Ask infra/runtime team).

Final quick status: this is a hand-scratchpad — capture more samples, try disabling cache, and escalate if reproducible. Keep rubric small and use it to tag tickets so we can prioritize consistent fixes.

-- end of scratchpad (still messy)
